_note: Ceilings are PREREGISTERED: they are written before the next change, not fitted to it. Raising one is a deliberate commit with a reason -- the same rule this skill applies to thresholds. The unit is estimated tokens at chars_per_token; the estimate is [H], the drift it catches is [K].
_runs_note: The file lists under `runs` are a reading of SKILL.md's procedure -- what a mode actually pulls into context -- not a measurement of a live session. They are [H] and they are the number that matters operationally, so they carry their own ceilings.

What remains is the rules themselves and is content, not commentary. Raised deliberately, each ~3% above the new measurement: T1 7400->7900, T2 33700->36700, audit 11800->13100, registry-write 22400->24600, code-audit 14400->16500, recovery 14200->14900. T0 left at 300 -- it still has slack, and shrinking a ceiling that is not binding buys nothing. NOTE: the ceiling that caught this was doing its job on its own author; the first push of 1.10 went red here, which is the intended behaviour and is why the gate exists.
